# #1715: Patch: an unreadable game record is quarantined instead of wedging the statistics fold
Opened by @jgoetzmann-bot.

## What it actually means

The server periodically folds stored game records into the running card-statistics totals. The fold reads a batch, and if even one stored record cannot be parsed — an old row written before the current format, or drift between deploys — the entire batch is abandoned, and abandoned again on every later pass: the bad row sits at the head of the queue forever and nothing behind it is ever counted. The same unreadable row also makes the record-listing endpoint fail. After the change, the unreadable row is set aside with an alert naming it, the rest of the batch is counted, and statistics keep flowing.

## Why

`game_records_fold_pending` selects a `FOR UPDATE SKIP LOCKED` batch ordered by id and parses every row before marking any folded; a single parse error aborts the transaction (`crates/server/src/db/pg.rs:4656-4687`). The head-of-line poison row is retried on every retention pass (`api/retention.rs` logs `game_records.fold_failed` and retries), blocking every record queued behind it. `game_records_list` parses identically, so the same row 500s that read (:4645-4650). Migration 0041's folded check keeps the poisoned row permanently — the purge only empties folded rows. Reachability: `game_records_insert` validates at write, so poison needs pre-0041 rows — exactly the rows this fold exists to consume — or schema drift across deploys.

## Proposal

Per-record isolation: catch the parse error per row, mark that row folded (or set a quarantine flag) with a `game_records.fold_poison` alert naming its id, and fold the rest of the batch. Skipping a row that can never parse is strictly better than letting it block all later rows.

## Where it lands

`crates/server/src/db/pg.rs`, `crates/server/src/db/store.rs` (trait), `crates/server/src/db/fake.rs`, `crates/server/src/api/retention.rs`; tests in `crates/server/tests/store/contract.rs` (the harness already has a raw-SQL escape hatch, `StoreHarness::forget_game_record_folds`, for planting a bad JSONB row). Spec §9.11, R1044000.

## Acceptance criteria

- A planted malformed record does not stall the batch: every later row folds.
- The poisoned row is marked (never retried) and its id logged or alerted.
- `game_records_list` no longer fails on the quarantined row (or explicitly excludes it).
- Contract test covers the case; fake store keeps its current contract.

## Size and risks

Small-medium. Decide quarantine-vs-mark-folded: marking folded loses the record, but an unparsable one is uncountable either way — an alert keeps it visible. The pg-only path naturally lives in the Docker contract suite; the fake can no-op or emulate via a flag.
